title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: priority of Mediator-decree vs elect-saving decree is hard speculation — execution-order is clear; eternal conception-order only God knows
pass_a_gloss: This argumentation calls us unto a speculation exceedingly difficult, and by no means fitted unto founding dogmatic Theology. For it leans upon consideration of Priority and Posteriority in those two decrees of the Divine will, concerning giving a Mediator, and concerning saving the elect, which both were conceived and established from eternity. As for what pertains unto me, I know that the order of execution, according to which God willed benefits to come unto men, can be delineated with no trouble: but in what order God held them sealed from eternity in his mind and will, let him alone presume to narrate who dares even to affirm that he has been with God from the secret and everlasting counsels.
pass_b_english: This argument calls us into a very hard speculation, poorly fitted to founding dogmatic theology. It hangs on priority and posteriority between those two decrees of divine will — giving a Mediator, and saving the elect — both conceived and established from eternity. As for me: I know the order of execution, by which God willed benefits to reach men, can be sketched with no trouble. But in what order he held them sealed from eternity in his mind and will — let only him presume to tell who dares claim he has been with God from the secret eternal counsels.
source_text: Haec argutatio vocat nos ad speculationem valde difficilem, et dogmaticae Theologiae fundandae minime accommodatam. Nicitur enim consideratione Prioritatis et Posterioritatis in illis duobus voluntatis Divinae decretis, de dando Mediatore, et de electis servandis, quae utraque ab aeterno fuerunt concepta et constituta. Ad me quod attinet, scio ordinem exsecutionis, secundum quem Deus voluit beneficia ad homines pervenire, nullo negotio posse delineari: at quo ordine Deus ea consignata tenuit ab aeterno in mente ac voluntate sua, is solus enarrare praesumat qui se Deo ab arcanis et aeternis consiliis fuisse etiam affirmare audeat.
